name: red-team

findings.message: CMBR-1 skip guard requires `_start_iter -gt 1`, so when a run is interrupted during iter 1 (`_persisted_iter=1` → `_start_iter=1`) the condition is false, `_cid_resume_first_iter` stays false, and already-complete cycle members in that iteration are re-dispatched instead of being skipped — the most common interruption point is unprotected.

The `iter > 0` guard fires unconditionally on every cycle member dispatch in every run (fresh and resume alike), because `iter` is sourced from `for (( iter=_start_iter; … ))` where `_start_iter >= 1` and `_cycle_iter_dispatch` is never called with `iter=0`; the design notes (Gap 7) explicitly flag this exact guard as WRONG, state it violates GUAR-1 by changing fresh-run event sequences, and require its removal — but it was not removed.
findings.quote:
if [[ "$iter" -gt 0 ]]; then
            eb_emit_event "stage.start" "stage=$s" \
                || { local _r=$?; warn "eb_emit_event stage.start failed (rc=$_r, continuing — disk/perm/lock?)"; true; }
        fi

findings.message: Every CMBR-1 assertion sets up `current_iter=2` (interrupted on iter 2); the case where a run is interrupted on iter 1 (`current_iter=1`, `_start_iter=1`) is never exercised, so the logic error in Finding 1 produces no test failure.

No test asserts that `stage.start` is NOT emitted for cycle members on a fresh run, so the unconditional `stage.start` emission in Finding 2 is invisible to the test suite; GUAR-1 has no enforcing test on the cycle-member side.
